title: WSU vs WWU: tuition, size, accreditation
summary: Washington State University (WSU) versus Western Washington University (WWU). Also searched as WWU vs WSU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Western Washington University (WWU) and Washington State University (WSU) are both public institutions located in the state of Washington, but they differ in several key aspects. WWU is situated in Bellingham and has an undergraduate enrollment of approximately 13,544 students, whereas WSU is located in Pullman with a larger undergraduate population of about 21,099. Tuition for in-state students at WWU is $9,582, which is lower compared to WSU's in-state tuition of $13,391. These differences reflect variations in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance between Western Washington University (WWU) and Washington State University (WSU), notable differences emerge in tuition and student debt. For in-state students, WWU charges $9,582 in tuition, which is less than WSU's in-state tuition of $13,391. Out-of-state tuition is also slightly lower at WWU, with a cost of $28,707 compared to WSU's $29,950. Regarding student debt, the median amount owed by graduates who complete their degrees is $18,500 at WWU, while WSU graduates have a median debt of $19,500. These figures highlight the relative affordability of WWU in terms of tuition and median debt compared to WSU.

Overall, WWU vs WSU presents a scenario where WWU tends to be more economical for both in-state and out-of-state students, with slightly lower tuition fees and median debt upon graduation. This cost comparison is an important consideration for prospective students evaluating their higher education options within Washington state.

sections.heading: Pick WWU if
paragraphs: Pick Western Washington University (WWU) if you prefer a public institution with a high admission rate and a relatively affordable tuition for in-state students.
